name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean after redistricting points strongly Republican
Jerry Carl holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.16M raised plus $547K outside support vs. $86K for Jones)
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 96% to win
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot, but no polling or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively Republican: a deep-red open seat, a dominant fundraising and outside-spending advantage for Carl, and markets pricing a Democratic win at only about 3 percent. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the forecast stays anchored to the district's lean.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Clyde Jones Jr. within single digits, or unexpected outside spending on his behalf, would be the first sign this is closer than the district's lean implies.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and the Republican side holds every visible advantage. Jerry Carl has raised about $1.16 million and benefits from roughly $547,000 in outside support, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised about $86,000 with no outside spending on his side. The district's partisan lean is R+17, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 3 percent chance.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing. All three point the same direction, making this a Safe Republican seat with only a small chance of an upset.
